halfLife.notes: Once- or twice-daily dosing. Renally cleared — dose adjustment in renal impairment. No significant hepatic CYP metabolism. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

activeMetabolite.notes: No active metabolite. Primarily renally excreted unchanged.

cypInteractions.switchingRelevance: Minimal CYP interactions — renally cleared. Fewer pharmacokinetic interactions than most antipsychotics. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

metabolicRisk.notes: Minimal weight gain — one of the more metabolically neutral SGAs. Better profile than olanzapine and risperidone for metabolic parameters. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

lai.notes: No long-acting injectable formulation widely available in Malaysia.

reboundPsychosisRisk.notes: Taper preferred over abrupt cessation. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

formulationNotes: Biphasic D2/D3 pharmacology: low doses (50–300 mg/day) predominantly block presynaptic autoreceptors — may improve negative symptoms and depression. Higher doses (400–800 mg) provide full postsynaptic D2 blockade for positive symptoms. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
specialConsiderations: Dose-dependent mechanism: low doses may worsen positive symptoms if used below therapeutic antipsychotic range — be explicit about the treatment goal when dosing.
QTc risk is moderate — ECG at baseline; more QTc prolongation than risperidone.
Very high prolactin elevation — similar to risperidone; monitor for hormonal side effects.
No CYP interactions — useful in complex polypharmacy.
Renal clearance — dose halving in moderate renal impairment (CrCl 10–30 mL/min).
